proposed_fix.description: Confirm packet loss on the path to the emailservice pod, then restart or reschedule the pod only if loss is localized to its node or pod.
steps: Compare emailservice inbound error rate and latency against other services on the same node to determine whether loss is pod-local or node-wide.
Check network receive/transmit errors and drops on the node and pod interface hosting emailservice (read-only: interface counters, kubectl describe, events).
Inspect emailservice socket and memory growth (E1/E5/E7) for connection buildup, e.g. count of established/time-wait sockets in the pod.
If loss is localized to the pod, request approval to delete the emailservice pod so it is rescheduled (ideally onto a different node).
If loss is node-wide, request approval to cordon the node and move emailservice off it; do not drain other workloads without separate approval.
After the change, verify emailservice latency-50/90 and inbound error rate return to baseline.
preconditions: Confirm emailservice has more than one replica or that brief unavailability is acceptable.
Verify the node has spare capacity to accept the rescheduled pod.
Get explicit human approval before deleting pods or cordoning nodes.
Capture current pod, node, and interface counter state for comparison.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node if it was cordoned and let the scheduler place pods normally; pod deletion is self-healing via the controller, and if the new placement is worse, reschedule back to the original node by removing any temporary node constraints.
